title: BBVA, the leading bank in the eurozone in quantum computing
excerpt: BBVA ranks fourth among 64 financial institutions worldwide in The Quantum Index Finance 2026, an international ranking that assesses their readiness for quantum computing. The bank is the highest-ranked institution in the eurozone. With a score of 61 out of 100 — more than double the median score of 26 points among the 64 institutions analysed — BBVA stands out for its adoption of this technology, advances in quantum security and research activity.
content:
The index, developed by The Quantum Index in collaboration with HorizonX, assesses the activities of banks, insurers, asset managers and other financial institutions based on six indicators grouped into three categories: talent (30%), research and development (40%) and technology adoption (30%). JPMorgan Chase tops the ranking, followed by HSBC and Wells Fargo, which share second place, and Mastercard in third. BBVA ranks fourth under the index's ranking system, which assigns the same position to institutions with equal scores.

Among the banks leading the way in this technology, BBVA has climbed to fourth place over the past year thanks to its quantum computing strategy, a long-term commitment that combines the development of technological capabilities with the exploration of financial applications and preparation for future cybersecurity risks.

The ranking recognises BBVA's strength in technology adoption, where it scores 72 out of 100, the third-highest score in the index, behind only JPMorgan Chase and HSBC. The bank also stands out for its 14 documented quantum technology use cases, placing it joint second worldwide alongside HSBC on this indicator.

In addition, BBVA ranks second among the 64 institutions analysed in quantum networks and security, thanks to its post-quantum cryptography programme, its participation as a founding member of the 'Quantum Safe Financial Forum,' and its work on quantum key distribution.

In research, BBVA's scientific publications have the highest impact in Europe, tied with HSBC, with studies covering areas such as portfolio optimisation, derivatives pricing and cryptography. The bank also has an extensive collaboration network, with 14 joint initiatives involving technology providers, universities and Spanish and European research consortia, placing it joint fifth worldwide in this category.

"Quantum computing is a technology with enormous potential to transform the financial sector, but its development requires a long-term vision. At BBVA, we are working to build the necessary capabilities and expertise, identify practical applications and prepare for the challenges posed by its evolution," said Escolástico Sánchez, Head of the Quantum team at BBVA.

This strategy is built around three pillars: specialised talent, collaboration with technology companies and research centres, and the development of business-related use cases. Since 2020, BBVA has explored more than ten applications of quantum technologies in areas such as portfolio optimisation, derivatives pricing and fraud detection.

As part of this commitment, BBVA, together with the Provincial Council of Biscay through Lantik, is promoting the third edition of 'Banks in Quantum Days,' an international event taking place from November 16 to 18 in Bilbao and Getxo.

The forum brings together representatives from the financial sector, technology companies and quantum computing experts to share advances and explore the opportunities and challenges this technology presents for banking, from business applications to cybersecurity. The initiative reinforces BBVA's commitment to collaboration and knowledge sharing to drive the development of these technologies.

In parallel, the bank is developing a roadmap to adapt its security systems to the threats that future quantum computers could pose, with the aim of moving towards a quantum-safe environment.
